hints.title: Pixel Recolor Contiguity Obstacle
hints.text: Recoloring all 4-directionally connected pixels sharing the start color requires avoiding infinite recursion when target color equals the original color. How can initial color comparison prevent cyclic recoloring?

hints.title: Connected Component Invariant
hints.text: Only propagate to adjacent pixels whose color strictly matches the original start pixel color, immediately replacing with the target color.

hints.title: Recursive Flood Traversal Procedure
hints.text: Record original color image[sr][sc]. If original color equals color, return image. Define a recursive helper on (r, c): if (r, c) is out of bounds or image[r][c] does not match original color, return. Assign image[r][c] = color, and recurse on (r-1, c), (r+1, c), (r, c-1), and (r, c+1).

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def floodFill(self, image: List[List[int]], sr: int, sc: int, color: int) -> List[List[int]]:
        orig_color = image[sr][sc]
        if orig_color == color:
            return image
        m, n = len(image), len(image[0])
        def dfs(r: int, c: int):
            if r < 0 or r >= m or c < 0 or c >= n or image[r][c] != orig_color:
                return
            image[r][c] = color
            dfs(r + 1, c)
            dfs(r - 1, c)
            dfs(r, c + 1)
            dfs(r, c - 1)
        dfs(sr, sc)
        return image
```

complexity.notes: Every connected pixel is recolored once, with recursion call stack bounded by M * N.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Failing to check orig_color == color creates infinite recursion loops.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place pixel recoloring avoids allocating visited arrays.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Early exit when starting pixel already equals target color.
